newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk minister says better Greece ties likely soon.
newsitem.headline: Turk minister says better Greece ties likely soon.

text.p: Turkish Foreign Minister Ismail Cem said on Thursday that "concrete developments" to improve relations with Greece could take place soon, after a U.S.-brokered agreement between the two rivals this week.
"There is a serious possibility of concrete developments in the coming days," Anatolian news agency quoted Cem as saying in a statement.
The two countries agreed at a NATO summit in Madrid on Tuesday to respect each other's rights and renounce use of force in their longstanding dispute over the Aegean Sea.
Ankara and Athens have long been at odds over the divided island of Cyprus, ethnic minorities and territorial rights in the Aegean, which last year brought the two countries close to conflict.
The agreement was welcomed in both countries, but officials said action was needed to back up the paper pledge. It was not clear what steps Turkey's Cem was referring to.
The six principles were agreed upon after a meeting between Cem and Greek counterpart Theodoros Pangalos, together with U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright.
